newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Aid workers said to withdraw from two Angolan towns.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers said to withdraw from two Angolan towns.

text.p: Relief agencies have withdrawn their staff from two towns in eastern Angola because of increasing security problems, aid officials said on Tuesday.

The officials, who declined to be identified, said a U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) plane took six foreign relief workers from the towns of Luau and Cazomba in easternmost Moxico province at the weekend.
Both towns are controlled by members of the former rebel group UNITA, and the withdrawal came after reports of troop movements after dark along Angola's eastern border with the former Zaire.
A WFP statement said men in civilian dress initially refused to allow the plane to leave and detained its passengers and South African pilots for several hours.

The Angolan government has been waging a three-week offensive in the country's northeastern provinces which it says is aimed against armed refugees who crossed into the area after the downfall of Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko.
But analysts said this was a pretext to retake diamond-rich territory under the control of UNITA.
The fighting is the worst since the Angolan government and the rebels signed a peace treaty in 1994 to end two decades of civil war.

Both sides joined a power-sharing government in April, but the former rebels still hold vast areas of the Angolan countryside, including the richest diamond areas in eastern Lunda Norte province, to the north of Moxico.
